detail.title: gh-12041 return 422 for batch delete with missing match fields
detail.body:
### What's being changed:

closes #12041. Batch delete throws a 500 when you leave out a required match field (`match.class` or `match.where`). That's just bad input, should be a 422.

The three nil-checks in `validateBatchDelete` returned a plain error, which the handler turns into a 500. The cases right below them (class not found, bad where filter) already return `NewErrInvalidUserInput` and get a 422 from #11497, so this just does the same for the missing-field checks. Messages stay the same. Added a table test that fails without the change.

One thing for you: went with 422 to match the other validation cases here, but 400 works too if you'd rather.

- [x] Documentation has been updated, if necessary. Link to changed documentation:

- [x] Performance tests have been run or not necessary.

## Pull request overview This PR fixes issue #12041, where a batch delete request that omits required match fields (`match`, `match.class`, or `match.where`) returned HTTP 500 instead of a client-error status. The three missing-field checks in `validateBatchDelete` previously returned a plain `errors.New`, which the REST handler maps to a 500. They now return `NewErrInvalidUserInput`, which the handler (`handlers_batch_objects.go:185-187`) maps to a 422 Unprocessable Entity — matching the adjacent validation cases (class-not-found, bad where filter) already fixed in #11497. Error message wording is preserved. **Changes:** - Replaced `errors.New(...)` with `NewErrInvalidUserInput(...)` for the three missing-match-field checks so they surface as 422 rather than 500. - Added a table-driven test asserting that nil match, empty `match.class`, and missing `match.where` all classify as `ErrInvalidUserInput`. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated no comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | usecases/objects/batch_delete.go | Missing required match fields now return `ErrInvalidUserInput` (→ 422) instead of a plain error (→ 500); wording preserved. | | usecases/objects/batch_delete_test.go | New subtest verifying the three missing-field cases classify as `ErrInvalidUserInput`. | I verified that `ErrInvalidUserInput`/`NewErrInvalidUserInput` are defined (`errors.go:64-76`), that the handler maps this type to 422, and that the `errors.Wrap(err, "validate")` wrapping in `deleteObjects` remains compatible with the `errors.As` assertion used in the new test (the pre-existing class-not-found test uses the same pattern). No issues were found. --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

  <pre>## Breaking Changes

## Namespaces

* Add counter for blocked namespace requests by @dirkkul in https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/pull/11721

* Namespaces: Match colon-containing user/group ids literally for global callers by @dirkkul in https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/pull/11868

## BM25 / BlockMax (BMW) rework

* fix(bm25): record max-impact pair on memtable BlockEntry by @amourao in https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/pull/11780

*Adds support for changing property's index types.*

## gRPC web
*Addds gRPC web endpoint.*

* feat: introduce `/grpc-web` endpoint by @tsmith023 in https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/pull/12024

pr.title: gh-12041 return 422 for batch delete with missing match fields
pr.body:
### What's being changed:

closes #12041. Batch delete throws a 500 when you leave out a required match field (`match.class` or `match.where`). That's just bad input, should be a 422.

The three nil-checks in `validateBatchDelete` returned a plain error, which the handler turns into a 500. The cases right below them (class not found, bad where filter) already return `NewErrInvalidUserInput` and get a 422 from #11497, so this just does the same for the missing-field checks. Messages stay the same. Added a table test that fails without the change.

One thing for you: went with 422 to match the other validation cases here, but 400 works too if you'd rather.

### Review checklist

- [x] Documentation has been updated, if necessary. Link to changed documentation:
- [x] Chaos pipeline run or not necessary. Link to pipeline:
- [x] All new code is covered by tests where it is reasonable.
- [x] Performance tests have been run or not necessary.
